eta.hero_title:
The AI workspace
for trade teams.
eta.hero_lede: Inquiries, customers, quotes and email, in one app with AI agents.
eta.statement: Sales teams jump between inquiries, customer files, quotes and cold emails all day. **LULUX ETA puts them in one app, with AI agents working right next to that business data.**
eta.showcase_body: Pin a customer and a quote to the conversation, then have LULUX look up prices, draft an English reply, or produce a quote or PI as a PDF.
eta.showcase_alt: LULUX ETA chat: the AI drafts an English reply using the pinned customer and quote
eta.steps_title:
Morning to evening,
all in one place.
eta.step1_title: Start the day on the dashboard.
eta.step1_body: New email, new inquiries, customers due for follow-up and LULUX's daily summary, all on one screen.
eta.step1_alt: LULUX ETA dashboard: today's email, inquiries, follow-ups and trends
eta.step2_body: List and board views, filtered by stage, country, owner or tag. Import CSV and Excel locally, with duplicate checks built in.
eta.step2_alt: LULUX ETA customer list filtered by stage, country and owner
eta.step3_body: FOB, CIF, CFR and more, multiple currencies, letterhead and logo templates, A4 PDF export, and straight into an email as an attachment.
eta.step3_alt: LULUX ETA quotation with incoterms, currency and PDF export
eta.step4_title: Hard questions go to a small team.
eta.step4_body: Put LULUX, Claude Code, Codex and others in one group. A lead assigns the work, members answer in turn, and the lead sums up the conclusion and next steps.
eta.step4_alt: LULUX ETA group chat: a lead agent assigns work and sums up
eta.step5_body: Drag nodes into multi-step workflows and run them daily, weekly or on any cron schedule.
eta.step5_alt: LULUX ETA workflow canvas with several agent nodes connected
eta.p1_body: Each account has its own profile and memory. Tell LULUX “remember…” to save something; keys, passwords and card numbers are refused.
eta.p2_body: Connect DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot, a local Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic API. Model requests go only to the service you set up.
eta.p3_body: LULUX is built in, and you can add command-line agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code from Settings to share the work.
eta.p4_title: Customers to cash, in one line
eta.p4_body: Follow-ups, product catalogue, quotes, a deal board, orders and payments. An accepted quote becomes an order in one click.
eta.p5_body: Works with Gmail, Outlook, QQ Mail, Tencent Exmail, NetEase Mail and more. Inquiries are flagged automatically; the AI only drafts, and nothing is sent until you confirm.
eta.p6_body: Run once, every N minutes, daily, weekly or on a cron expression, targeting a workflow or a single prompt.
eta.avatars_caption: Some of the agents that can join a group chat
eta.data_title:
Your data stays
where you put it.
eta.data1_body: On the desktop it stays on your machine; on LULUX Cloud it stays on your server, scoped by role, team and account.
eta.data2_body: API keys and mailbox credentials are stored encrypted; the interface only ever shows them masked.
eta.data3_body: The database is snapshotted every 24 hours, keeping the latest 7 by default.
eta.data4_body: The team server adds roles and permissions, an audit log and one-step handover when someone leaves.
eta.download_body: Free desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux. Teams can run their own LULUX Cloud server.
eta.license_body: LULUX ETA's source is public under the Business Source License 1.1, a source-available license that is not OSI-approved open source. Individuals and organisations may use it in production for free, including internal modifications; it may not be sold or redistributed for a fee, or offered as a paid hosted service. The LICENSE file in the repository is the authoritative text.
eta.next_body: Discover potential buyers from HS codes and customs bill-of-lading data.
eta.disclaimer: Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Qwen and other names are trademarks of their respective owners and are used here only to identify the corresponding third-party software. LULUX ETA is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by these vendors. Third-party agents are downloaded by your own computer from the public npm registry and are not distributed with LULUX ETA.
eta.modes_title:
One laptop,
or a whole team.
eta.modes_lede: The same features, two ways to run them.
eta.mode_desktop_lede: A desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux.
eta.mode_desktop_1: Data lives in a local SQLite database; you sign in with an offline account.
eta.mode_desktop_2: Nothing passes through a LULUX server. Model requests go only to the service you set up.
eta.mode_desktop_3: Close the window and it stays in the tray; schedules and mail sync keep running.
eta.mode_desktop_4: Automatic snapshots every 24 hours, and an optional local PIN lock.
eta.mode_cloud_lede: Deploy the server on your own machine (Docker or Node.js) and colleagues sign in to LULUX Cloud from the app.
eta.mode_cloud_1: Conversations run on the server: close the client and the work carries on; reopen it to pick up where it is.
eta.mode_cloud_2: Multi-user accounts with owner, admin, member and read-only roles, and data scoped by team and organisation.
eta.mode_cloud_3: Group chats where colleagues and agents work together, everyone watching the same run live.
eta.mode_cloud_4: Audit log, permission ceilings, usage reports and handover when someone leaves.

flow.hero_lede: Run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code and Grok CLI on the model you already configured in DeepSeek Harness.
flow.unofficial: An unofficial community plugin, independently developed and maintained. Not affiliated with, or endorsed by, DeepSeek.
flow.gateway_title:
No logins.
No keys handed over.
flow.gateway_body: The plugin puts a small gateway inside DSH. Each CLI starts with a token bound to that run, which only works against the gateway; the gateway forwards every call to the model DSH is already using.
flow.diagram_cli_sub: Claude Code · Codex · Gemini CLI · Qwen Code · Grok CLI
flow.diagram_label: Request path: the CLI calls the local gateway with a run-scoped token, and the gateway forwards to the model configured in DSH
flow.g1_body: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code and Grok CLI.
flow.g2_body: Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Gemini, with streaming, tool calls and token usage carried through.
flow.g3_body: The environment is built from an allowlist and every run gets a private config directory. Tokens are stored only as hashes and revoked when the run ends.
flow.g4_body: Read-only, ask, edit or full, mapped to each CLI's own flags. The Kernels page sets the ceiling; a workflow node can only ask for less.
flow.g5_body: As your chat agent, as a subagent, or as a node in a workflow, alongside DSH's own agents.
flow.g6_body: Detects installed CLIs and versions and installs missing ones into the plugin's data directory. Every tarball is checked against the lockfile before any install script runs.
flow.gateway_caveat: A CLI still runs as your OS user and can read whatever your user can read. For untrusted repositories, run DSH in an OS sandbox or as a separate user.
flow.session_alt: Choosing Claude Code as the chat agent in the kernel picker at the top of a DSH session
flow.workflows_body: Drag out a DAG in DSH Web: ten node types, success/failure and true/false edges, retries, timeouts, concurrency and budgets.
flow.canvas_alt: DSH-LULUX Flow canvas: a DAG of CLI nodes with a condition branch
flow.w1_body: Generate with AI drafts a workflow from one sentence, then lints it.
flow.w2_body: The run inspector shows input, output, trace and token usage per node. Cancel, resume after a restart, or re-run.
flow.w2_alt: Run inspector with per-node status and output
flow.w3_title: Every CLI, managed on one page.
flow.w3_body: The Kernels page shows whether each CLI is installed, its version, whether it uses the gateway or its own login, and its permission ceiling. Missing ones install from there.
flow.w3_alt: Kernels page: install status, mode and permission for each CLI
flow.r_body: Workflows written by the chat model, generated with AI or imported start as unreviewed, and won't run from any trigger until you approve them in the canvas.
flow.w4_body: From the canvas, from chat through model tools, on a cron schedule, or through a signed webhook.
flow.install_body: Requires DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0` and Node.js `>=22.15.0`. Restart DSH afterwards and DSH-LULUX Flow appears in the sidebar and in Settings.
flow.install_desktop: On DSH Desktop, replace `--profile web` with `--profile desktop`.
flow.install_build: A GitHub install compiles on your machine. If pnpm asks for `allowBuilds`, add the names it reports as described in the README, then install again.
flow.e1: The gateway listens on loopback only, checks the Host header and refuses any browser request.
flow.e2: Webhooks are HMAC-SHA256 signed, with a ±5 minute window and replay protection.
flow.e3: HTTP and notify nodes have SSRF protection; credentials are dropped on cross-origin redirects.
flow.e4: Script nodes are off by default and can only be enabled in the plugin config.
flow.e5: TypeScript strict mode, unit and integration tests, CI on Linux, macOS and Windows.
flow.e6: Secret-named fields are redacted in run records and tool output.
flow.limits: There are known limitations, such as images being dropped when forwarding and Windows CLI launch not yet verified end-to-end. The README has the full list.
flow.gfeat_title:
Keys stay in DSH.
The CLIs still work.

download.hero_lede: Pick your system. Installers bundle their own runtime, so there's no Node.js or database to install.
download.recommended_mac_unknown: We can't tell which chip your Mac has. Not sure? Open the Apple menu → About This Mac: if it says Chip: Apple, choose Apple silicon; if it says Processor: Intel, choose Intel.
download.recommended_mobile: LULUX ETA is a desktop app. Open this page on a Windows, macOS or Linux computer to download it.
download.recommended_unknown: We couldn't detect your system. Please choose an installer below.
download.label_server: Team server package (server, web UI and deployment files)
download.checksums_body: Every release ships a `SHA256SUMS.txt`. After downloading, check it with:
download.fallback_title: Go straight to the releases page
download.fallback_body: We couldn't load the latest release from GitHub right now (a network problem or rate limit). The files below are from when this site was built; the releases page always has the newest version.
download.static_note: These are the release files from when this site was built. With JavaScript on, the newest version on GitHub is shown automatically.
download.unsigned_body: Preview installers are not yet code-signed (no Authenticode certificate on Windows, no Apple Developer ID notarisation on macOS). Everything works, but your system will warn you the first time you open the app. Only download from the official releases page, and check the SHA-256.
download.mac_1: macOS 14 and earlier: in Applications, Control-click LULUX ETA → Open → Open. You only need to do this once.
download.mac_2: macOS 15 and later: double-click once (it will be blocked), then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, find “LULUX ETA was blocked” near the bottom, click Open Anyway and enter your password.
download.mac_3: If macOS says the app “is damaged and can't be opened”, run this once in Terminal, then open it again:
download.win_1: When “Windows protected your PC” appears, click More info → Run anyway, then follow the installer.
download.win_2: If your browser says the file isn't commonly downloaded, choose Keep → Keep anyway in the downloads list.
download.linux_1: Make the AppImage executable, then run it:
download.linux_2: Requires FUSE 2 (Ubuntu 22.04: `libfuse2`; Ubuntu 24.04: `libfuse2t64`). The install guide covers other cases.
download.server_body: Each release includes a server package, or you can pull the Docker image. The server must sit behind an HTTPS reverse proxy.
download.requirements: Once installed, the app checks GitHub Releases for updates (on macOS you currently download new versions by hand).
download.emulation_note: There is no native ARM64 build for Windows yet. The x64 installer runs via emulation on Windows on ARM.
